description: RiskScape is a risk modelling engine that assesses risk to people, buildings and infrastructure from natural hazards such as volcanic eruptions, earthquakes, landslides, tsunami and floods. It was developed by New Zealand's Institute of Geological and Nuclear Sciences (GNS Science) and National Institute of Water and Atmospheric Research (NIWA), now combined as Earth Sciences New Zealand. Users define their own risk calculations as pipelines tailored to the hazard and input data, run them in expert, standalone or shared cloud setups, and create custom outputs with Python; an example on the site evaluates roads exposed to flooding with losses computed every 10 square metres of the network and summed by region. The engine is installed from a zip file following the documentation, which covers pipelines, data manipulation and Python functions. The site describes RiskScape as open source, but the pages read show an all-rights-reserved notice and no licence text, so terms should be confirmed with the provider. Caveats: bundled data and examples are New Zealand focused and models must be configured by the user. It serves hazard exposure, loss and resilience analysis of infrastructure networks, emergency response scenarios and climate adaptation planning, and is comparable to the OpenQuake Engine and CLIMADA catalogued here.
